rationale: Lycopolitan habitual aspect prefix for 3sg.m, recurring six times on this page (lines 16, 18, 20, 23, 24, 25-26, 27, 30) in the iterative description of what the Illuminator habitually does. Should be added to the dialect-features section as a regular Lycopolitan equivalent of standard Sahidic ϣⲁϥ-.

Reduplicated verbal form on ⲱⲗ 'carry, lift' with directional ⲁⲃⲁⲗ. Soteriological action: the Illuminator 'draws/lifts (them) out of fear' (line 27), parallel to ⲃⲓ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ in lines 20, 24, 26. Confidence moderate.
Lycopolitan ⲥⲟⲣⲁⲍⲧ = ⲥⲱⲣⲁϩⲧ̄ 'be at rest, calm, still' (Crum). Substantival 'rest, repose,' paired with ⲣⲏⲛⲏ (εἰρήνη) 'peace' as the second of the seven goods (lines 23, 27).
Standard Coptic ϣⲧⲟⲣⲧⲣ̄ 'disturbance, trouble.' The cosmic agitation that fills men's hearts during the night, dispelled by the Illuminator's coming.

Lycopolitan reflex of ϩⲟⲣⲟⲧⲉ 'fear' (cf. ⲑⲣ̄ⲧⲉ in same passage line 24). Synonym/variant of the standard ⲑⲣ̄ⲧⲉ; both attested on this page within five lines, suggesting they are interchangeable in this dialect.

Variant of ⲛⲓⲁⲛⲟⲩⲣ̄ⲱⲉ 'the Watchers/Sleepless Ones' (already in glossary) — here in lower-case earthly register: human night-watchers who guard encampments. The Illuminator's coming makes their watch unnecessary because his light dispels fear and darkness.

proposed_english: shines forth / shall shine forth / which shines forth
rationale: Recurring forms of the verb ⲡⲓⲣⲉ/ⲡⲣⲓⲉ 'shine, radiate' (same root as ⲡⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ 'the Radiance' in glossary), used five times on this page (lines 9, 13, 16, 19, 32). Preserves the active-emission verbal sense per correspondential principle.
